answers.note: Thorough, well-sequenced plan with named retrieval starters, two checkpoints, predict/modify/make tasks and an assessment that tests exactly what was taught.

Sensible sequence with retrieval starters, but the only formal checkpoint comes late (Lesson 10), while loops are never taught, a list lesson is squeezed in, and the assessment is described only vaguely.
Good see-modify-make approach and a well-matched assessment, but lessons give a focus rather than clear objectives, and retrieval and checkpoints are only generic or loosely implied.
Excellent ladder from predict and trace to modify, make, debug (infinite loop and off-by-one) and challenges, with test cases, staged hints and correct, verified solutions.

Solid tasks and correct solutions, but it jumps quickly from a small modify step to writing from scratch, gives students few expected outputs or test cases, has hints on only two tasks, and the debugging task sits in an optional extension.

Well-structured predict-investigate-modify-make sequence with a strong three-bug debugging task and good hints, but there is no real stretch task beyond a one-line extension, and the task set is thin for an hour.
Clear non-specialist instructions, answers and collection steps, but the short-answer worksheet would take most classes well under the 35 minutes allotted, leaving too little work for 50 minutes.
Good, well-timed consolidation tasks with full answers and early-finisher work, but what should be handed in or completed is left vague ('collect the books or sheets', 'leave the work').
Very complete cover pack with a word-for-word script, timings, a no-enzymes approach, a scaffolded writing task, full answers and a clear hand-in with a note for the returning teacher.
